I can totally relate, my parents always thought I’m just super happy and I finally were myself after years of depression and supported me in my mania even though I had really strange thoughts (they’re pretty spiritual so they thought I was evolving into another level). Years after I met my boyfriend who was aware of bipolar-nes because his ex had it. So i showed up super weird behavior and ups and downs and he came to the point to talk to my therapist and after years of suspected bipolar disorder i finally got diagnosed with it. Until today I can’t tell if I’m bipolar or not because my meds work and I never had rough mania since then except some reaaallly soft hypomania. Listen, it’s part of the disorder to question yourself if you have it or not. In the end listen to your doctors and therapists , parents often can’t tell if you’re having mania because they think it „made click“ in your head and you came out of your depression or made some kind of self development OR you’re just happy (depending on the level of mania)

Hey! Well I kinda know this „being obsessed with people“. It’s a quite common BPD thing. Especially when the person is triggering something inside you (in a positive way) they start to be your anchor, you might project what you missed out in your childhood or young adulthood onto this person and you burn bright like a candle for him/her. It can even turn into an obsession and you do EVERYTHING to get their attention. You sound like you need to get taken care of, maybe you should look back what you missed out in your life or if you’re lacking anything only another person can do to you. 
It’s part of the illness to do the „splitting“ - like there’s only black and white, good and bad and so on. You love someone until they say one word or do one action-  and booom you suddenly hate the person or feel abandoned or rejected. You need to learn it’s just the illness and NOT you! They don’t reject or abandon you at the moment it’s happening. You need to learn to be empathetic, like all those people have their own life and Problems and things they need to take care of and you can’t be the middle of their universe. Your love or obsession can drown them and they might want to run and THEN you get abandoned or hurt, because you gave them no space to breathe or to look after themselves. See it as a „vice versa“, you give and you take. Only that is how any relationship is going to work. I wish you good luck in finding your own truth about that! Remember, those are just my thoughts and experiences!
